AgileMark addresses a growing cybersecurity gap: sensitive information captured directly from the screen. What began with mobile phone photography is now expanding with smart glasses and other wearable cameras, creating new visual data-loss risks that traditional security controls were not designed to manage. AgileMark is a cybersecurity solution developed by Agile Momentum Pte. Ltd. , a Singapore-based company founded in 2018. The company focuses on screen watermarking, visual accountability, and behavioral risk deterrence for enterprises handling sensitive and regulated information. Traditional Data Loss Prevention controls are effective across digital channels such as email, USB, file transfer, applications, and networks. However, once information is legitimately displayed on an authorized user’s screen, external cameras operate outside those channels. AgileMark helps organizations address this exposure through adaptive screen watermarking, text and graphic watermarks, and symbolic identifiers designed to create accountability while minimizing disruption to legitimate users. Rather than claiming to detect photo-taking, AgileMark focuses on deterring the behavior before it occurs . Its solutions are used across sectors including financial services, government, telecommunications, and other security-sensitive enterprises in Southeast Asia . AgileMark’s mission is to help organizations reduce visual data exposure by extending security awareness and accountability to the last visual mile — the screen itself.

Ansteroid, commercialises advanced mobile security research originating from the Centre on Security, Mobile Applications and Cryptography (CRPO) at Singapore Management University. Our mission is to give security teams visibility into what mobile applications actually do at runtime — beyond the reach of conventional static scanners and emulator-based tools. We build deterministic, on-device analysis technology purpose-built for the realities of modern Android environments. Our flagship platform, FA³ (Fine-Grained Android Application Analysis) , delivers deep, multi-layer runtime tracing across the Java, ART, JNI, and native layers of an application — running on real, unrooted handsets without modifying the target app. FA³ is deterministic rather than machine-learning-based, meaning its findings are precise, repeatable, and explainable. Its five core strengths — on-device, non-invasive, ART-aware, multi-layer, and fine-grained — make it uniquely suited to high-assurance environments where accuracy and defensibility matter. FA³ is already deployed with a leading Singapore security agency. Our second technology, Outsight , extends this philosophy of non-invasive observation to an entirely new dimension. Using external CPU side-channel monitoring, Outsight detects real-time, in-app user actions without any modification to the target application and without root access. Working like a one-way mirror — the application runs unaware on one side while Outsight reads every action from the outside — it opens new possibilities for behavioural analysis, monitoring, and assurance where traditional instrumentation is impossible. Together, FA³ and Outsight represent a new generation of mobile security capability: rigorous, deterministic, and grounded in world-class academic research, yet engineered for real-world operational deployment. Ansteroid partners with government agencies, financial institutions, and enterprises seeking trustworthy insight into mobile application behaviour.

You already own a GRC platform. It holds the control library, the risk register and the audit trail, and it does that job well. What it does not do is check whether a control is working today. It sits between the operational systems and the GRC platform, takes the control objectives already defined there, and turns them into tests that run on a schedule. The platform connects to cloud accounts, identity providers, endpoints, databases and on-premises systems. Collectors are agentless and read-only, so nothing is installed and nothing is changed. Checks go past the cloud API layer into operating system, virtual machine and database configuration, which is where most control failures actually sit. Results go back into whatever system of record the customer already uses, whether that is ServiceNow, Archer, LogicGate or a spreadsheet. There is no migration and no second dashboard to keep current. Every test run is timestamped and hashed, and the system call behind each result is recorded alongside it. When an auditor asks how a result was produced, the answer is already on file. The control tests are written for the frameworks that apply in this region: IM8, the Cybersecurity Code of Practice for CII 2026, MAS TRM, BNM RMiT, BOT, BSP, Thai PDPA and ISO 27001. Zeroport is a cybersecurity company that makes critical systems physically unreachable from the networks people connect to. Incorporated in Singapore in 2026, Zeroport builds Fantom, a hardware-enforced, non-IP remote access platform for organisations that cannot afford a breach: power utilities, banks, semiconductor fabs, government agencies and defence. The problem it solves has become the industry's most exploited weakness. Remote access is unavoidable: engineers, vendors and contractors must reach systems they cannot stand in front of. Yet every mainstream method, VPN, ZTNA, RDP, PAM and VDI, runs on TCP/IP. That leaves an internet-reachable endpoint at the trust boundary, and security becomes a race to patch faster than attackers write exploits. Fantom removes that boundary rather than defending it. Only keyboard and mouse signals travel into the protected network; only an encrypted video stream comes out. Inside, two isolated system-on-chip domains are separated by a unidirectional buffer with optical isolation, so files, clipboard content and packets have no path to cross. There is nothing routable to scan, and nothing to patch. Around that isolation sits the governance regulators expect: identity federation with mandatory multi-factor authentication, approval workflows, time-bound vendor access, a keyboard firewall that terminates sessions on forbidden commands, and full session recording with immutable logs streamed to SIEM and SOAR. Fantom's design follows the zero-trust principles set out in NIST SP 800-207, and its isolation and session-audit controls help operators evidence obligations under frameworks such as IEC 62443. It goes to market across Asia Pacific through systems integrators who embed Fantom as their standard remote access layer.
